genesis.34.p1.b1.text: Now Dinah, the daughter Leah had borne to Jacob, went out to visit the daughters of the land.

genesis.34.p1.b2.text: When Shechem son of Hamor the Hivite, the prince of the region, saw her, …

genesis.34.p1.b3.text: … he took her and lay with her by force.

genesis.34.p1.b4.text: And his soul was drawn to Dinah, the daughter of Jacob. He loved the young girl and spoke to her tenderly.

genesis.34.p2.b1.text: Get me this girl as a wife.

genesis.34.p2.b2.text: Jacob heard that Shechem had defiled his daughter Dinah, … he remained silent about it until they returned.

genesis.34.p2.b3.text: Meanwhile, Shechem’s father Hamor came to speak with Jacob.

genesis.34.p2.b4.text: When Jacob’s sons heard what had happened, they returned from the field. They were filled with grief and fury, …

genesis.34.p3.b1.text: My son Shechem longs for your daughter. Please give her to him as his wife.

genesis.34.p3.b2.text: You may settle among us, and the land will be open to you. Live here, move about freely, and acquire your own property.”

genesis.34.p3.b3.text: Demand a high dowry and an expensive gift, and I will give you whatever you ask. Only give me the girl as my wife!”

genesis.34.p4.b1.text: But because Shechem had defiled their sister Dinah, Jacob’s sons answered him and his father Hamor deceitfully.

genesis.34.p4.b2.text: To give our sister to an uncircumcised man would be a disgrace to us.

genesis.34.p4.b3.text: … that you become circumcised like us—every one of your males. Then we will give you our daughters … and become one people.

genesis.34.p4.b4.text: But if you will not agree to be circumcised, then we will take our sister and go.”

genesis.34.p5.b1.text: The young man, who was the most respected of all his father’s household, did not hesitate to fulfill this request, because he was delighted with Jacob’s daughter.

genesis.34.p5.b2.text: These men are at peace with us. Let them live and trade in our land; indeed, it is large enough for them.

genesis.34.p5.b3.text: Will not their livestock, their possessions, and all their animals become ours?

genesis.34.p5.b4.text: All the men who went out of the city gate listened to Hamor and his son Shechem, …

genesis.34.p6.b1.text: Three days later, while they were still in pain, two of Jacob’s sons (Dinah’s brothers Simeon and Levi) took their swords, …

genesis.34.p6.b2.text: … took Dinah out of Shechem’s house, and went away.

genesis.34.p6.b3.text: Jacob’s other sons … looted the city, because their sister had been defiled. They took their flocks and herds and donkeys, …

genesis.34.p6.b4.text: They carried off all their possessions and women and children, and they plundered everything in their houses.

genesis.34.p7.b1.text: You have brought trouble upon me by making me a stench to the Canaanites and Perizzites, the people of this land. We are few in number; if they unite against me and attack me, I and my household will be destroyed.

genesis.34.p7.b2.text: Should he have treated our sister like a prostitute?
